desc: Write `Solution.maxProduct` using 2D DP arrays `reach[par][prod]` and `nonempty[par][prod]` as Python int bitsets over sum offset `[−S, S]`, with `mask = (1 << (2*S+1)) - 1`.
Initialize `reach[0][1] = 1 << OFFSET` (empty subsequence) and `nonempty` all zeros.

For each `x` in `nums`, build `next_reach` and `next_nonempty` as copies, then loop over `par ∈ {0,1}` and `prod` 1..limit, shifting the bitset by `+x` if `par==0` else `−x` (mask and bounds), multiply product, and OR into the appropriate new parity/product entries; also OR from `nonempty` bitset.

In the same per-`x` pass, handle the "start new subsequence" case: set `start_par = 0` (even index 0), `start_prod = x` (if `x <= limit`), shift `+x`; OR `(1 << (OFFSET + x))` into `next_reach[0][x]` and into `next_nonempty[0][x]`.
After processing all elements, scan `prod` from `0..limit` and both parities; if `(nonempty[par][prod] >> (OFFSET + k)) & 1 == 1`, update `ans = max(ans, prod)`.
Return `ans` if found, else `-1`; also add an early return `-1` when `abs(k) > sum(nums)`.
Verify with given examples and a few edge cases (single element, zeros, limit < smallest product).
